    //==
    // # ISurface, IClosedSurface, ISolid, IConvexSolid
    //
    // These marker interfaces already exist (surfaces-solids.concepts.plato):
    // ISurface and ISolid inherit only IGeometry3D, IClosedSurface and IConvexSolid only
    // another marker. They add no members over their bases, and IGeometry3D's own
    // derived helpers live in the geometry package (P5). No curve/surface-specific
    // function is derivable for them here without new members, so none is offered.
    //==
    // # Deformation bodies for the control-net and sampled surfaces
    //
    // The IDeformable3D obligations of the surfaces in `surfaces.types.plato`
    // that are spanned by stored points: every position is carried through the
    // mapping, and the parameter-domain data — weights, knots, degrees, the
    // subdivision scheme and level — passes through untouched. Exact for an
    // affine mapping; under a nonlinear one the result is the surface over the
    // moved net, not the image of the original surface.
    //
    // The generated surfaces (revolve, extrude, rule, loft-by-curve, sweep,
    // tube, offset) are absent: each stores an axis, a direction, a distance or
    // a generator curve, none of which a point mapping can carry. So is
    // HeightField, whose samples are elevations over a fixed XY grid rather than
    // free positions.

    // Every corner carried through the mapping.
    Deform(self: BilinearPatch, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): BilinearPatch
        => (mapping(self.P00), mapping(self.P10), mapping(self.P01), mapping(self.P11));
```

    // Each cross-section deformed in turn; the sections keep their point counts,
    // so the loft's correspondence between them survives.
    Deform(self: LoftedSurface, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): LoftedSurface
        => (self.Sections.Map(section => section.Deform(mapping)), self.Closed);
```

    // The control mesh deformed; the scheme and refinement level are not
    // geometry. The limit surface of the deformed mesh, which for an affine
    // mapping is the deformed limit surface — subdivision is affine-invariant.
    Deform(self: SubdivisionSurface, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): SubdivisionSurface
        => (self.ControlMesh.Deform(mapping), self.Scheme, self.Levels);
}
